FOREWORD
Indian by the by the

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part III ) was adopted by the Standards Institution on 15 April 1977, after the draft finalized Solid Mineral Fuels Sectional Committee had been approved Chemical Division Council.
0.2 This standard now consists of three parts as follows: and Part I Coal and its preparation, Part II Coal sampling and analysis, Part III Coke.

The glossary of terms reIating to coal and its preparation, earlier covered in IS : 3810-1966* now forms Part I of this standard and is being revised with a view to aligninit with IS0 1213 ` Vocabulary of term responsible for relating to solid mineral fuels ,.a The Sectional Committee the preparation of this standard decided to enlarge the scope by including the terms reIating to coal sampling and analysis ( Part II ) and coke ( Part III ). 0.3 This standard consists of a list of terms commonly employed in coke industry. Terms relating to sampling and analysis of coal, covered in Part II of the standard, may also be applied for coke with suitable modification, wherever necessary and have, therefore, not been covered here to save repetition. In this standard some of the terms have their equivalents shown in brackets; use of such equivalents is deprecated.

2.2.3 Grading ( Screening ) - The commercial operation of sorting coke between two screens, by causing one component to remain on the screen through which the other components pass. 2.2.4 Hand Shaking -The operation in which hands and is given a horizontal oscillatory motion 75 mm. a sieve is held in the with a throw of about

2.2.5 Hand Placing - The operation in which the screen remains stationary and each piece of coke is handled; if a piece, in some position and without forcing, passes through the screen aperture it shall be considered as under size. 2.2.6 agitated Mechanical Sieving - The by mechanical means. operation in which a set of sieves is

2.2.7 Struck LevellingA method of levelling the coke surface in a container when determining bulk density, whereby a straight edge is slid across the top of the container, any piece of coke which touches the straight edge being removed. 2.3 Physical Properties rubbing of 2.3.1 Abrasion -Particle size reduction caused by the pieces of coke against each other or against a hard surface. 2.3.2 Breakage -- Particle size reduction resulting 2.3.3 Shutter Index --The stated aperture after being 1354- 1964* ) . percentage of coke retained subjected to the shatter test

2.3.6 Relative Density (Apparent ) - The ratio of the mass of a volume of dry coke of any size to the mass of an equal volume of water at a specified temperature. 2.3.7 Porosity --The volumetric proportion of voids within a piece of coke.
